label: Dark matter: Planck CMB lensing
note: Planck lensing convergence: how much mass bends the CMB light on its way to us, summed along the line of sight. Most of that mass is dark matter. Orange = more mass than average, blue = less. Wiener-filtered and smoothed 1.5°, so only the large-scale pattern is real; grey is masked (Milky Way and point sources).

label: Galaxy density, nearby universe (2MRS)
note: Where the ~41,000 galaxies of the 2MASS Redshift Survey sit, smoothed over 3°. Galaxies trace the dark-matter cosmic web out to ~400 Mpc. The empty band is the Milky Way blocking the view.

label: Dust reddening E(B−V) (SFD)
note: Schlegel-Finkbeiner-Davis dust reddening: how much our own galaxy dims and reddens everything behind it. Bright = look through with care.

label: CMB temperature (Planck)
note: Planck CMB temperature: the leftover glow of the Big Bang, 380,000 years after it. Red is slightly warmer, blue slightly colder (about ±0.0003 K).

label: Planck 30-70 GHz colour
note: Planck low-frequency instrument, 30/44/70 GHz in colour: CMB fluctuations plus galactic synchrotron and free-free emission.

label: Planck 100 GHz
note: Planck 100 GHz, near the CMB peak: the CMB pattern everywhere except the galactic plane.

label: Gamma-ray sky (Fermi-LAT colour)
note: Fermi-LAT gamma rays. The bright band is our own galaxy; the dots are blazars and pulsars.

label: Gamma rays 3-300 GeV (Fermi)
note: Fermi-LAT 3-300 GeV, the highest-energy band: the galactic plane, the Fermi bubbles above and below the galactic centre, and blazars.

label: Gamma rays 100-300 MeV (Fermi)
note: Fermi-LAT 100-300 MeV: dominated by cosmic rays hitting interstellar gas.

label: MeV gamma rays (COMPTEL)
note: COMPTEL 0.8-30 MeV: the gap between X-rays and Fermi, dominated by the inner galaxy.

label: IceCube 10-year excess
note: IceCube 10-year tracks above ~3 TeV: places with more events than average for their declination, dark at 1σ to bright at 4σ. With no trials correction most bright spots are chance; that is the point of the reproduction.

label: X-ray sky (ROSAT)
note: ROSAT all-sky survey, 0.1-2.4 keV: hot gas in our galaxy, supernova remnants, galaxy clusters and active galaxies.

label: X-ray sky 2-20 keV (MAXI)
note: MAXI on the Space Station, 2-20 keV: X-ray binaries along the galactic plane and the brightest active galaxies.

label: Milky Way, visible light
note: The Milky Way in visible light (Mellinger panorama). Dark lanes are dust blocking starlight.

label: Gaia DR3 colour
note: Gaia's 1.8 billion stars rendered by brightness and colour.

label: Galactic dust (Planck 857 GHz)
note: Planck 857 GHz: cold dust in our galaxy glowing in far-infrared.

label: Planck 353-857 GHz colour
note: Planck high-frequency instrument in colour: cold dust filaments threading the galaxy.

label: Polarised dust (Planck)
note: Polarised dust emission: dust grains line up with the galactic magnetic field.

label: Far infrared (IRAS)
note: IRAS 12-100 μm, reprocessed (IRIS): warm dust, star-forming regions and the zodiacal glow of our solar system.

label: Far infrared (AKARI)
note: AKARI 65-140 μm in colour: dust heated by young stars.

label: Neutral hydrogen (HI4PI)
note: HI4PI 21-cm survey: the column of neutral hydrogen gas. The Magellanic Stream trails below the plane.

label: Hydrogen by velocity (LAB)
note: Leiden/Argentine/Bonn HI survey coloured by Doppler shift: gas moving towards (blue) and away (red).

label: Ionised hydrogen (H-alpha)
note: H-alpha composite: gas ionised by hot young stars and supernova shocks.

label: Ionised hydrogen (WHAM)
note: Wisconsin H-Alpha Mapper: the faint warm ionised gas that fills the galaxy, at 1° resolution.

label: Radio 408 MHz (Haslam)
note: Haslam 408 MHz: synchrotron from cosmic-ray electrons spiralling in the galactic magnetic field. The arc is the North Polar Spur.

label: Polarised synchrotron (Planck)
note: Polarised synchrotron from Planck: traces the direction of the galactic magnetic field.
